compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: Samuel comes to Bethlehem with a heifer, consecrates Jesse’s family, learns not to judge by appearance, and anoints David.
observations.label: A sacrifice creates the setting for David’s anointing

observations.body: The passage presents fear, public sacrifice, consecration, hidden son, divine seeing, and anointing as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: fear, public sacrifice, consecration, hidden son, divine seeing, and anointing

observations.body: The passage places sacrifice and selection beside fear, public sacrifice, consecration, hidden son, divine seeing, and anointing.
observations.label: sacrifice and selection

payload.posture: Read 1 Samuel 16:1–13 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the sacrificial gathering is the setting for selection, not the reason David is chosen
payload.title: A sacrifice creates the setting for David’s anointing
